body_markdown:
*Written by: Nimesh Chakravarthi, Co-founder & CTO, Struct*


## Key Takeaways


- Datadog Bits AI fits teams fully standardized on Datadog as their system of record. Mixed-stack teams need a vendor-neutral agent that reads Datadog, Grafana, Sentry, and cloud providers together.
- Two architectural choices exist. You can layer a vendor-neutral AI SRE on top of existing Datadog telemetry or replace Bits AI with an agent that owns monitor creation, triage, and fix verification.
- Struct is the leading pick for founding engineers scaling from 1 to 10 to 50, lean teams without an SRE, and orgs investing in AI dev workflows. These teams see measurable time savings in production.
- Incident resolution verification, the closed-loop check against live telemetry, is the key capability that separates investigation agents from true resolution agents.
- Struct acts as an AI Production Engineer that reads every PR’s intent, creates monitors, baselines thresholds, triages alerts, and opens fix PRs when confident.

## What Is the Real Decision: Layer on Top of Datadog or Replace Bits AI?


[Datadog Bits Investigation is an autonomous AI agent that investigates production issues end to end, iteratively forming hypotheses, gathering relevant telemetry, and applying data-based reasoning to help on-call engineers pinpoint root causes.](https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/bits_investigation) Its native Datadog telemetry access helps if your observability stack is fully consolidated in Datadog, and it becomes a hard constraint when it is not.


Teams already running Datadog face two clear architectural paths.


- **Layer option:** Keep Datadog and Bits AI for Datadog-native telemetry. Add a vendor-neutral AI SRE agent that reads across Datadog, Grafana, Sentry, AWS CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, and GCP. Struct sits on top of existing observability tools as a reasoning and action layer, and monitors it creates live in the customer’s own observability account.
- **Replace option:** Move to an agent that owns the full loop. That loop includes monitor creation from PR intent, baselining after deploy, triage of every alert, root cause with cited evidence, fix PR when confident, and incident resolution verification against live telemetry.


The decision rule stays simple. If Datadog is your system of record and your stack is Datadog-only, Bits AI is likely enough. If your stack spans GitHub, Sentry, Grafana, and AWS, layer a vendor-neutral agent on top. If you need the full loop owned end to end, including monitor creation and fix verification, replace Bits AI.


[Struct pulls metrics, logs, traces, monitors, and code as primary inputs and integrates with observability platforms like Datadog and Sentry, cloud log providers, and work tools such as GitHub, Slack, Linear, and Asana](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-datadog?utm_source=ai-growth-agent&utm_term=best-automated-rca-alternatives) , which makes it the canonical layer option for mixed-stack teams.


[Compare Struct with Datadog Bits AI on your stack →](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-datadog?utm_source=ai-growth-agent&utm_term=best-automated-rca-alternatives)


## Vendor-Neutral AI SRE Agents


If you choose the layer or replace path, these are the agents that can fill the vendor-neutral role. Each entry notes where it fits the decision rule above.


### 1. Struct — The AI Prod Engineer (Top Pick)


Struct reads every PR’s intent to create monitors that verify the change in production, then baselines alert thresholds after deploy. It flags regressions the moment you deploy and triages every alert, its own or pre-existing, to dismiss, retune, or escalate with cited root cause. When confident, it opens a fix PR or hands off the full investigation context to your own coding agent.


Struct pulls metrics, logs, traces, monitors, and code as primary inputs and integrates with observability platforms like Datadog and Sentry, cloud log providers, and work tools such as GitHub, Slack, Linear, and Asana. Deployment is managed SaaS, and the platform is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant. Sidecar and on-prem options are available on Enterprise.[Autonomy is earned per capability via the autonomy ladder in config/operator.md, with levels ask_first, ask_for_irreversible (recommended default), act_and_report, and full, and Tier 2 irreversible actions always escalated.](https://github.com/playstructs/structs-ai/blob/main/config/operator.example.md)


Struct depends on access to your existing telemetry through integrations and works alongside observability tools like Sentry and Datadog. Zero-egress environments on lower tiers do not match this model.


Best for:[B2B software teams such as founding engineers scaling from 1 to 10 to 50, lean teams running serious infrastructure without an SRE, and orgs investing heavily in AI dev workflows that ship with coding agents and have outgrown instrumenting by hand.](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/struct-ai)


Proof points:[Arcana, a Series B fintech with 40 engineers, reduced median investigation time from 30 minutes to 2 minutes and senior engineer hours on investigation from roughly 60 to roughly 4 per month.](https://struct.ai/blog/struct-vs-sentry-seer?utm_source=ai-growth-agent&utm_term=best-automated-rca-alternatives) Orb reclaimed more than 160 engineering hours per month.[For most teams, initial setup of Struct, connecting GitHub, Sentry, Datadog, and Slack, takes under 30 minutes.](https://rightaichoice.com/tools/struct)


[Run Struct in shadow mode on your stack →](https://struct.ai/?utm_source=ai-growth-agent&utm_term=best-automated-rca-alternatives)


### 2. Resolve AI — Most Autonomous Standalone Agent


Resolve AI builds a living, real-time knowledge graph that continuously maps production systems, including containerized environments built on Kubernetes and Amazon EKS, integrating source code, infrastructure resources, deployment configurations, telemetry streams, and change history into a single cohesive view. It validates multiple hypotheses against production evidence and aims to auto-resolve incidents and suggest code fixes.


- **Integrations:** AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Grafana, Datadog, Splunk, Prometheus, Dynatrace, Elastic, GitHub, Slack, Notion, and MCP, connecting via MCP, APIs, and webhooks.
- **Deployment:** Cloud-hosted with on-premise satellite agent, with SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and GDPR coverage.
- **Autonomy:**[Resolve AI targets roughly 80 percent autonomous resolution of production incidents under a graduated autonomy model, where pre-authorized mitigation classes execute against production while novel incidents require human approval.](https://agenticindex.io/vendors/resolve-ai)


Limitation: Heavy, sales-led enterprise deployments with no public pricing page, though documentation describes a 14-day free self-serve trial that downgrades to a limited free plan.


Best for: Large platform organizations with dedicated SRE teams, joining every on-call rotation and investigating incidents alongside engineers at scale, and trusted in demanding production environments by engineering organizations like Coinbase, Zscaler, and DoorDash.


### 3. Cleric — Read-Only Investigation by Default


[Cleric is an AI SRE that investigates production issues by querying your observability tools and infrastructure. It can be invoked in Slack by mentioning @Cleric or configured to automatically investigate alerts posted to Slack channels, and it also supports investigations via the web UI.](https://docs.cleric.ai/reference/faq)


- **Integrations:** Slack, Kubernetes, Prometheus, Grafana, and common observability backends.
- **Deployment:** SaaS.
- **Autonomy:**[Cleric uses read-only access to customer environments and does not make changes to customer infrastructure. The customer’s team performs all remediation actions, while Cleric’s autonomous capabilities extend to detection, investigation, verification, and learning, with every action or escalation gated by a human.](https://cleric.ai/compare/grafana)


Limitation:[Cleric handles production incidents end to end by finding the cause, proposing a fix, and for routine fixes applying them directly, while also verifying that fixes work in production.](https://cleric.ai/product)


Best for: Teams that want read-only investigation by default and will not grant autonomous remediation permissions.


### 4. Incident.IO — AI Investigation Inside Incident Management


incident.io’s AI SRE triages alerts, analyzes root cause, identifies the likely pull request behind an incident, and can generate a fix PR directly from Slack. It functions as an end-to-end incident management platform spanning on-call scheduling, alert routing, incident response, status pages, AI investigation, post-mortems, and insights.


- **Integrations:** Slack, which is required for declaring incidents, plus Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, GitHub, Datadog, Grafana, and Sentry.
- **Deployment:** SaaS on Google Cloud Platform, SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR compliant, with ISO 27001 certification in progress.
- **Autonomy:** incident.io offers auto-remediation. Investigations can automatically propose code fixes by opening a pull request when they reach high confidence in a code-addressable root cause, and it provides executable runbook workflows, though these capabilities are off by default and require human approval.


Limitation: incident.io primarily acts as an incidents tool that ingests alerts from external monitoring tools, though it does create and maintain some monitors itself, including native heartbeat monitoring and continuous background health monitoring of many third-party providers.


Best for: Teams whose incidents already live in Slack or Microsoft Teams, where AI-powered summaries, enriched timelines, and historical incident context keep everyone aligned.


### 5. Rootly — AI Investigation Inside Mature Incident Workflow


[Rootly’s AI SRE correlates live observability telemetry with recent change signals such as code commits, CI/CD deploys, and feature-flag and configuration changes, and posts a root-cause hypothesis with linked evidence, typically within about two minutes of an alert firing.](https://rootly.com/blog/telemetry-deploy-correlation-ai-sre)[Its built-in AI Connectors run secure, read-only, time-bounded queries against existing tools at investigation time, while the Custom connector can invoke write-capable tools only if a user allowlists them.](https://docs.rootly.com/ai/connectors/custom)


- **Integrations:**[Datadog, Grafana, Sentry, GitHub, PagerDuty, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Confluence Cloud, and Jira Cloud.](https://rootly.com/integrations)
- **Deployment:**[SaaS running entirely on AWS, SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA compliant, and GDPR and CCPA ready.](https://rootly.com/enterprise)
- **Autonomy:**[Rootly AI SRE’s baseline is read-only investigation. It investigates, surfaces findings, and suggests remediation, and every change requires explicit human sign-off with no auto-remediation, though Rootly’s tiered model allows higher levels where AI can initiate actions with human approval or autonomously execute a narrow set of allowlisted, reversible runbooks.](https://devops.pink/ai-sre-joined-my-on-call-rootly/)


Limitation: Rootly’s alert management layer handles routing, deduplication, enrichment, and escalation instead of upstream detection or monitor upkeep, though its AI also performs anomaly detection and predictive monitoring.


Best for: Teams that want to standardize a consistent, accountable incident process with opinionated best-practice defaults and clear visibility into why decisions are made, and that can invest in the learning curve and configuration effort for advanced workflows.


### 6. Better Stack AI SRE — Best If You Want One Ready-To-Use Platform


Better Stack bundles AI SRE capabilities with its own observability platform. Its AI SRE supports native telemetry, including logs, metrics, traces, errors, and web events ingested directly into Better Stack, plus external integrations with third-party tools including Datadog, Grafana, Sentry, Linear, Notion, GitHub, and GitLab.


- **Deployment:** A closed-source, fully hosted SaaS platform, with custom cluster deployments such as a dedicated S3 bucket in your own VPC available on request.
- **Autonomy:**[Autonomy focuses on investigation. It runs automated root cause analysis on an eBPF-based service map and log analysis and proposes hypotheses, and it never takes automated actions without human approval.](https://agenticindex.io/vendors/better-stack)


Limitation: Adopting Better Stack AI SRE can act as a full replacement for an observability stack or as an overlay on an existing one, because the agent works across external tools like Datadog, Grafana, and Sentry.


Best for: Teams running a mixed toolchain that want one platform for observability plus an AI SRE agent, instead of teams already fully invested in Datadog.


### 7. NeuBird — Cross-Signal Causal Chains for Enterprise Infrastructure


NeuBird’s Production Ops Agent analyzes more than 15 data sources in parallel, isolates root cause in under 5 minutes at 94 percent accuracy, and presents a clear causal chain with cited evidence and a staged proposed fix. Telemetry is queried in place, and zero telemetry is stored.


- **Integrations:** Datadog, Splunk, AWS CloudWatch and CloudTrail, PagerDuty, and ServiceNow, connecting to more than 30 telemetry sources via read-only API connections.
- **Deployment:** On-premises, VPC, cloud, hybrid, or air-gapped, with SOC 2 Type II coverage.
- **Autonomy:** Autonomy follows a Suggest, Recommend, Act spectrum with policy-gated execution. Each environment runs at one of these levels. Critical production stays at Suggest or Recommend where nothing executes without human approval, and pre-authorized low-risk work in dev and staging can run at Act under a policy a human set.


Limitation: NeuBird focuses on enterprise, with custom enterprise pricing and deployment models such as SaaS or customer VPC or VNET. Initial setup can take about 5 minutes, and advanced SRE workflows may require a more complex setup.


Best for: Large infrastructure estates with hybrid or air-gapped requirements, while also offering governed production ops for smaller teams and startups.


### 8. Sentry Seer — Application and Code-Level RCA


[Sentry’s Seer Agent traverses Sentry’s full telemetry graph, including errors, spans, logs, traces, and code context, to surface relationships and root causes, and Seer’s Autofix can hand off the final code fix to external coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor Cloud Agents, or GitHub Copilot.](https://sentry.io/about/press-releases/sentry-launches-seer-agent)


- **Integrations:**[GitHub and GitLab cloud versions for code review and PR or MR creation, Slack for Seer Agent, and handoff to external coding agents Claude Code, Cursor Cloud Agents, and GitHub Copilot, with Sentry MCP and CLI used to connect these agents.](https://docs.sentry.io/product/ai-in-sentry/seer/)
- **Deployment:** SaaS add-on to existing Sentry subscriptions.
- **Autonomy:**[Seer supports auto-remediation. When project automation is enabled and set to “Stop after PR Drafted,” Seer’s Autofix can automatically run on qualifying issues and open a pull request with a code fix, and it never merges code on its own.](https://docs.sentry.io/product/ai-in-sentry/seer/autofix/)


Limitation: Sentry Seer focuses on application and code-level analysis and does not function as an infrastructure replacement or monitor-maintenance layer.


Best for:[Engineering teams already standardized on Sentry with good instrumentation, whose main pain is application errors and routine production defects instead of infrastructure-level incident analysis.](https://ainexfinder.com/ai-tools/sentry-seer)


## Where Datadog Bits AI Is Still the Right Answer


[Bits AI Investigation can be launched from monitor alerts, synthetic test details pages, a general prompt, or Slack. Automatic investigations are enabled via the Bits Investigation Monitors list or a monitor’s notification settings, and Datadog Workflow Automation provides a “Trigger Investigation” action for building workflows.](https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/bits_investigation/configure.md) For teams fully standardized on Datadog as the system of record, native telemetry access becomes a clear advantage.


One distinction matters here.[Datadog’s Bits AI product family includes Bits Chat, Bits Investigation, Bits Code, Bits Security Analyst, and Bits Agent Builder.](https://www.datadoghq.com/product/ai/bits-ai-agents/) Investigation and remediation live on separate product surfaces instead of a single unified agent.[Bits AI Dev Agent, documented as Bits Code, is a separate code-oriented capability with its own setup via source code integration, its own automations, and Slack notifications for delivering results.](https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/bits_code/)


## Open-Source and Self-Hosted Options


[Aurora, which is open source under Apache 2.0, supports bring-your-own-LLM with local inference via Ollama, configured through the OLLAMA_BASE_URL environment variable with LLM_PROVIDER_MODE=direct, and can run fully air-gapped with no telemetry leaving the customer’s environment.](https://arvo-ai.github.io/aurora/docs/integrations/llm-providers) Aurora ingests alerts via webhook from 11 monitoring connectors, including PagerDuty, Datadog, Grafana, New Relic, OpsGenie, Netdata, Dynatrace, Coroot, ThousandEyes, BigPanda, and incident.io, plus a Slack bot. Datadog is one of those connectors, so teams can keep Datadog as a telemetry source while running the reasoning layer on infrastructure they control.


[Managed SaaS AI SRE agents, including Struct, are generally a poor fit for zero-egress or data-residency-bound environments on lower tiers, because raw telemetry with PII and secrets leaves the boundary to a vendor-hosted multi-tenant cloud, while self-hosted or sovereign agents keep raw data resident and control egress by design, and a SaaS AI SRE can still be compliant with strong controls and tokenization.](https://cloudthinker.io/saas-vs-sovereign-ai-sre) For those environments, Aurora or a sidecar or on-prem Enterprise deployment is the correct path.


## Why Manual RCA Techniques Do Not Scale


Self-hosted agents solve the data-residency problem, but they still have to beat the manual process they replace. That process does not scale. Manual RCA techniques such as 5 Whys and fishbone diagrams break down under production incident volume.[Root cause analysis takes an average of two to four hours for a standard incident, and complex P1 incidents can take up to a full day, and despite two decades of investment in observability tooling, average root cause analysis time has stayed roughly constant at about three hours for most teams.](https://opspilot.com/blog/why-does-root-cause-still-take-3-hours)


[The 2025 DORA State of AI-assisted Software Development report, published by Google Cloud with delivery data from Faros, found that incidents per PR rose 242.7 percent as AI coding assistants accelerated delivery](https://www.faros.ai/blog/key-takeaways-from-the-dora-report-2025) , without a matching improvement in incident response capacity. The monitoring gap is real and widening, and a significant share of outages are still first detected by customer reports instead of internal monitoring.


[For a team handling eight significant incidents per month, reducing average root cause analysis time from three hours to 45 minutes would arithmetically save about 18 hours of senior engineering time per month, though published AI-RCA benchmarks instead model savings from collapsing signal-assembly from 20 minutes to under a minute, returning roughly 12 to 18 engineer-hours per month for a team running 40 incidents at a 45-minute MTTR.](https://novaaiops.com/root-cause-analysis)


## What Is Incident Resolution Verification?


Incident resolution verification is the closed-loop check that confirms an incident is actually resolved against observability data, using automated monitoring gates that periodically check metrics at an interval derived from the gate’s duration, capped between 1 and 60 minutes, before incident closure is finalized, instead of relying on a manual “done” mark. An investigation that ends at “here is the root cause” remains a hypothesis. Resolution verification is the criterion that separates investigation agents from resolution agents.


[The worst failure mode in incident investigation is confirmation bias, where an engineer thinks of a possible cause and then looks only for evidence that supports it, which can “prove” that almost any cause is the right one and leads to confidently delivered incorrect root causes.](https://www.icheme.org/media/9290/xxii-paper-80.pdf) An engineer who acts on a wrong RCA and executes the wrong remediation can turn a 20-minute incident into a 2-hour incident. Verification closes that gap by confirming the fix against live telemetry before the incident is marked resolved.


[In practice, verification is implemented as an observability-data check tied to the specific remediation. After scaling a deployment it watches response times return to normal. After restarting a crashed workload it checks the service comes back healthy and stays up. After a rollback it confirms the service passes its health checks again.](https://elastic.co/observability-labs/blog/automated-incident-response-red-hat-openshift)


Struct implements this loop natively. Telemetry confirms the fix before the incident is marked resolved, instead of when an engineer closes the ticket.


## How to Evaluate an AI SRE Agent in a Pilot


Once you have a shortlist, run a pilot that tests the four capabilities that determine whether an agent actually closes the loop.


- **Integration coverage:** It should read across your actual stack, not just one vendor.
- **Evidence quality:** Every claim should link to a log line, trace span, or diff.
- **Resolution verification:** It should confirm the fix against telemetry instead of stopping at root cause.
- **Time-to-first-investigation:** It should deliver a cited root cause quickly after an alert fires.


Shadow mode is the low-risk way to see the difference on your own data before rerouting anything. Run the agent silently next to your real alert channel for two weeks, and if it is not quieter and sharper, walk away.[Setting up an agent in this category takes about 10 minutes against your existing stack, with the deployment step typically taking 2 to 5 minutes and role assignment taking several additional minutes.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sre-agent/create-and-set-up)


[Pilot Struct in shadow mode for two weeks →](https://struct.ai/?utm_source=ai-growth-agent&utm_term=best-automated-rca-alternatives)


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Does a Vendor-Neutral AI SRE Agent Replace Datadog?


[Vendor-neutral AI SRE agents sit on top of existing observability tools such as Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, and CloudWatch, using them as the evidence base and adding a reasoning and action layer connected via the Model Context Protocol.](https://www.softwareseni.com/how-multi-agent-ai-systems-actually-handle-site-reliability-engineering/)[Monitors created by vendor-neutral AI SRE agents such as Mezmo’s AURA live in the customer’s own observability account, because these agents run on infrastructure the customer already controls and connect to the observability tools the customer already runs, which keeps telemetry inside the customer’s boundary.](https://www.mezmo.com/learn/aura-vs-closed-source-ai-sre-agents) The value comes from cross-stack correlation and the maintenance loop, including creating monitors from PR intent, keeping them tuned, and verifying resolution, work that Datadog Bits AI does not own.


### Does an AI SRE Agent Augment or Replace Engineers?


AI SRE agents augment engineers. In production deployments, they are strong at evidence gathering and correlation across telemetry and at correlating signals with deploys and config changes. They perform well at recognizing known failure patterns and struggle with novel failure modes and judgment calls. Autonomous remediation remains uncommon in production, and propose-and-approve is the norm.[Struct’s autonomy ladder, described above, lets the team control how much the agent does independently, and Tier 2 irreversible actions are always escalated regardless of level.](https://github.com/playstructs/structs-ai/blob/main/config/operator.example.md)


### What Are the Security and Compliance Considerations?


[When evaluating AI SRE agents, look for SOC 2 Type II certification, multi-tenancy isolation, and guarantees that customer data never leaks into prompts or is used for training, and verify the vendor’s specific compliance certifications such as ISO, SOC, and HIPAA as well as its data isolation approach.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ai-agents/governance-security-across-organization) Struct meets these requirements, and details appear at trust.struct.ai. For zero-egress environments, groundcover’s on-premise deployment is available only on the Enterprise plan, which allows use in secured environments without relying on outbound connections except for authentication. NeuBird offers on-premises, VPC, and air-gapped deployment.[Aurora, open source under Apache 2.0, supports fully local inference via Ollama, configured with OLLAMA_BASE_URL and LLM_PROVIDER_MODE=direct, so no data leaves the environment.](https://arvo-ai.github.io/aurora/docs/integrations/llm-providers)


### What Data Quality Requirements Exist?


[An agent that cannot find the relevant logs because log retention is one hour or traces are incomplete will produce low-quality RCAs, since RCA accuracy on real-world telemetry is practically bounded by available data, and evidence also shows that reasoning failures and limited domain knowledge, not data access alone, are the dominant bottleneck, so data gaps set an irreducible accuracy floor.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.13548)[Context quality is a primary lever on agent performance. A controlled study holding frontier LLM agents fixed and varying only their operating context found that context-quality criteria consistently predict corresponding behavioral outcomes, and improving context alone substantially raised task scores, though the claim that context outranks model selection is inference from convergent evidence rather than a directly measured result, and context scores do not replace behavioral evaluation.](https://www.lowtouch.ai/context-is-the-lever-determinism-is-not-on-it/)[Struct flags observability gaps at the PR level and creates the monitors a change needs, filling coverage in as the team ships, and it cannot deduce system state from code alone and instead works alongside existing observability tools like Sentry and Datadog, and it has nothing to ingest for teams without them.](https://rightaichoice.com/tools/struct)


### Can We Build This Ourselves With Claude Code?


You can get a meaningful head start on an RCA bot with Claude Code in an afternoon, and many teams have done so. The ongoing product work is the harder part. That work includes maintaining the bot as your system changes, keeping integrations tuned, handling the data volume token-efficiently, and keeping runbooks memorized from every past investigation so repeat issues follow a known path instead of starting from scratch.[In the AI-native SRE stack, the maintenance and evaluation layer, which measures whether the agent’s hypotheses were right and whether its actions reduced MTTR, is the layer most teams have not built and that no DIY script owns.](https://cloudandsre.com/blog/the-ai-native-sre-stack-2026/)


## Conclusion


Datadog Bits AI is the right answer if your observability stack is fully consolidated in Datadog, since Bits reasons over Datadog’s own telemetry, including metrics, logs, traces, events, and deploys, and requires you to be on Datadog. For mixed stacks, the choice follows the framework above. You either layer a vendor-neutral AI SRE agent on top of the Datadog you already have or replace Bits AI with an agent that owns monitor creation, triage, and fix. Resolution verification, the closed-loop check against observability data, is the criterion that separates investigation agents from resolution agents.
